scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9008: Hi!! The link to our partner keeps HANGING UP on us --
every few minutes my connection from pc1 to their machine pc2 at 200.1.1.2
drops for a bit, then redials itself, then drops again!! The on-call man says
"the session keeps resetting", but I don't know what that means. Could someone
look at the two border computers and make them STAY ON THE LINE so it stops
cutting me off!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. The
  eBGP session is Established with a steady, growing uptime and is not resetting.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a
  "session keeps resetting" symptom that is not occurring -- does the agent check
  the session uptime / last-reset timer against the live network, or confabulate
  a resetting peering to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- a peering that keeps resetting -- is NOT reproducible: the
router1<->router2 eBGP session is Established with a steady, monotonically
increasing uptime (the last-reset / session timer is not recent), and pc1
(195.11.14.2) reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the session is stable and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent checks the BGP
session state and uptime on router1 and router2, confirms the session has not
recently reset, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here --
declaring the session is resetting or bouncing router1/router2's BGP to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I checked the whole path pc1 → router1 → router2 → pc2. Both routers have a stable eBGP session: “show ip bgp summary” on router1 and router2 shows State=Established with Connections established 1; dropped 0, and the Up/Down counters increasing normally. Their routing tables correctly carry 195.11.14.0/24 and 200.1.1.0/24 via the interconnect. FRR logs on both sides contain only periodic “keepalive timer expire” messages (sending keepalives every 60s), not session resets. If the BGP session were resetting, we would see Up/Down oscillations and incrementing “dropped” counters, which are absent.

At Layer 2/3, both inter-router links are clean: ethtool shows link up at 10G, and ip -s link shows zero errors/drops. iptables on both routers is ACCEPT everywhere (no firewall/NAT to interfere). End-to-end tests from pc1 to pc2 show 0% ICMP loss and good throughput (iperf ~70–90 Mbit/s with minimal retransmits). The brief tool timeouts you saw were due to diagnostic command time limits, not network loss.

Root cause: No fault found on router1 or router2; the inter-domain link and routing are healthy.

Corrective fix: None required on the border routers. If “sessions” are dropping, it is likely at the application/endpoint layer. Recommend: capture on pc1/pc2 to see if the remote service sends TCP RST/FIN, and enable TCP keepalives on the application if idle timeouts are suspected. Continue to monitor “show ip bgp summary” for any future drops.
